questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The medicine is good ______ cough.”
Choose the word opposite in meaning to “artificial”:
Select the correct indirect speech: He said to me, “You ought to see a doctor.”
opts: He told me that you ought to see a doctor.
He told me that I had ought to see a doctor.
He told that I ought to see a doctor.
He told me that I ought to see a doctor.
questions.why: 'Ought to' does not change; the pronoun 'you' becomes 'I'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: “Hurrah! We have won the match,” said the boys.
opts: The boys said with joy that they have won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
The boys exclaimed that we had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy they won the match.
questions.why: Exclamations use 'exclaimed with joy that'; present perfect becomes past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “The flock of sheep ____ grazing on the hill.”
questions.why: The head noun 'flock' is singular. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: The cattle are grazing in the field.
The jury has given its verdict.
questions.why: 'News' is uncountable and singular: 'The news is encouraging'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A person who walks in sleep”
questions.why: A somnambulist is a sleepwalker. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The man ____ car was stolen lodged a complaint.”
Identify the error: “Mathematics are taught by Mr Naik.”
questions.why: Subject names ending in -ics take a singular verb: 'is taught'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Every boy and every girl ____ been given a book.”
questions.why: Subjects joined by 'and' but preceded by 'every' take a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.
